NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (connector material upgrade or protective coating) to physically block corrosive ion ingress.  
Departure: A chemically active surface treatment that forms a sacrificial ion-exchange layer, capturing chloride ions before they reach contact points.  
This works because electrochemical corrosion requires ion mobility; the layer binds chloride ions, reducing local electrolyte conductivity and disrupting the corrosion cell.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Corrosion current density (i_corr) = i_0 × exp((2.303×F)/(R×T) × (E_corr - E_pass)) where i_0 is exchange current, F is Faraday's constant, R is gas constant, T is temperature, E_corr is corrosion potential, E_pass is passivation potential.  
Magnitude verification: For a 0.1 V shift in E_pass due to chloride binding, i_corr decreases by ~50% (typical for passive films), sufficient to mitigate drift per datasheet corrosion rates.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Instrument: pH sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "stated telemetry feed")  
- Instrument: Conductivity probe (ALREADY-RECORDED: "stated inspection record")  
- Material: Ion-exchange polymer coating (DERIVED: "stated spec" for connector material compatibility)  
- Procedure: Electrochemical deposition (DERIVED: "stated physics" for thin-film adhesion)  
- Input stream: pH (ALREADY-RECORDED: "stated telemetry feed")  
- Input stream: Conductivity (ALREADY-RECORDED: "stated inspection record")  
- Reference threshold: pH 8.5 (DERIVED: "stated physics" – alkaline pH inhibits corrosion by shifting E_pass)  
- Reference threshold: Conductivity < 50 µS/cm (DERIVED: "stated data" – baseline from "stated inspection record")  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard practice (connector-level modification, no new structural work)  
- Operability: No change (passive treatment, no active controls)  
- Maintenance: Same class (coating lifetime matches standard practice material upgrade)  
- Cost: Same class (polymer coating cost ≅ premium connector material)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Monitor VSWR and conductivity simultaneously during coastal exposure.  
Pass/fail: VSWR must not exceed 1.5:1, and conductivity must stay < 50 µS/cm for 6 months.  
Duration: 180 days.  
Kill criterion: "Mechanism is falsified if VSWR drift exceeds 0.1 from baseline within 180 days."  
Validation: Uses "stated inspection record" data for baseline conductivity.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: VSWR (per problem statement, defines failure threshold). Secondary indicator: conductivity supplements by confirming electrolyte activity.  

DESIGN_POINT  
The mechanism acts through a 0.1 V shift in passivation potential, reducing corrosion current density by ~50%, sufficient to keep VSWR drift < 0.1 per datasheet corrosion rates.  

EPO PROBLEM SOLUTION BIND  
(a) CLOSEST PRIOR ART: Standard practice uses stainless steel or gold-plated connectors to resist corrosion via passive film stability.  
(b) DISTINGUISHING FEATURE: The ion-exchange layer actively binds chloride ions, preventing their participation in corrosion reactions, unlike passive barriers that only delay ion ingress.  
(c) OBJECTIVE TECHNICAL PROBLEM: Prevents chloride accumulation at contact points, which passive coatings cannot fully stop in high-salinity environments.  
(d) WHY THE OBVIOUS KNOB FAILS: Thicker coatings or harder materials trap chlorides at interfaces, accelerating localized corrosion; the ion-exchange layer eliminates the corrodant at the source.
